scenePromptTest.title: Scene Prompt Comparison Test
scenePromptTest.subtitle: Enter one scene or story text only, then generate the current baseline plus three new scene-design strategies to compare whether AI can infer style, story direction, and the best reusable scene by itself.
scenePromptTest.sceneInputPlaceholder: Example: On the night before a young martial monk leaves the mountain, his master speaks to him in the temple courtyard and sends him to find a missing old friend. Morning mist is heavy, and the mountain road beyond the old wooden gate leads toward an unknown town. Later storyboards need farewell, descent from the mountain, looking back at the temple gate, and a mentor-student turning point.
scenePromptTest.empty: Four comparison images and full prompts appear after generation.

sceneReferenceTest.title: Scene Multi-view A/B Test
sceneReferenceTest.subtitle: Independently test how single-view scene references and multi-angle scene boards affect storyboard generation. Character asset, storyboard prompt, and model stay fixed; only the scene reference changes.
sceneReferenceTest.characterUrlPlaceholder: Or paste a character asset image URL
sceneReferenceTest.scenePlaceholder: Example: rainy temple backyard at night, stone floor, old wooden door, lanterns under the eaves, bamboo forest in the distance, wet reflections.
sceneReferenceTest.stylePlaceholder: Example: low-saturation wuxia film mood, humid air, cold cyan moonlight, warm lantern rim light.
sceneReferenceTest.standardBoardDescription: Always generates front, reverse/back, and top-down views for A/B testing against the single-view baseline.
sceneReferenceTest.storyboardPlaceholder: Example: A monk stands in the center of a rainy temple backyard at night, slightly turned toward the old wooden door, medium shot, quiet restrained emotion.
sceneReferenceTest.emptyScenes: Scene reference results appear after generation.
sceneReferenceTest.emptyComparison: Storyboard results appear after running A/B comparison.
sceneReferenceTest.needCompareInput: Upload a character asset, generate scene references, and enter the shared storyboard prompt.
